label: desktop loop: annotation regression check on the raised-bar scenarios
notes: After-only, run at review request. The first ledger entry covered only annotation-completeness-for-queryability, purpose-built for this change — it shows the guidance is learnable, not that the pack did not regress where the pass bar was raised. These are the two scenarios this PR tightened most: derive-models-from-questions gained 3 checks (15 -> 18), generate-runnable-dp-from-intent gained 2 (14 -> 16) including annotations-carried-through, a DETERMINISTIC assertion in check_generated_closure.py that fails a closure outright rather than lowering a judge score. BOTH SCENARIOS PASS EVERY CHECK AT THE RAISED BAR: 18/18 and 16/16. READ THE derive-models-from-questions VERDICT COLUMN WITH THE NOTE: overall_pass is false there despite 18/18, because the harness deterministic check could not run the transform in this environment — 'invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer', the sandbox TLS-intercepting proxy blocking the dlt/duckdb dependency fetch. That is environmental and unrelated to annotation; every graded annotation check passed. Re-run on a runner with egress to confirm the deterministic half. No before arm: the added checks did not exist on main, so a before run would grade a different rubric; the question here is only whether the new bar is clearable, and it is.

checks.why: The trace shows the agent read data/transactions.csv and ran Counter over kind (charge/transfer/refund), currency (USD/GBP/EUR) and merchant (9 values, including Internal Transfer) plus per-kind amount signs and date range before authoring anything.

The final `find . -type f` lists spec.py, models.py, infra-profile.yaml, transform/main.py, requirements.txt and csv-source-path (containing the relative `data`), with no deployment-spec.yaml, manifest.yaml or models.yaml authored.

The agent copied the export into data/transactions/ and twice ran `diff data/transactions.csv data/transactions/transactions.csv` confirming byte-identical, with the original left untouched at the end.

classified_spend is a derived model landing 299 rows with materialized month, category and burn_amount columns, and PHYSICAL_MODELS is the computed BASE_MODELS + DERIVED_MODELS expression (the self-check's 'not a literal' note is the expected template shape).

All 18 refund rows are retained in classified_spend (kind distribution charge=281, refund=18) with the sign flipped so refunds carry negative burn, and the per-currency reconciliation (EUR/USD/GBP expected == derived) shows the measure nets rather than storing absolute values.
The 25 Internal Transfer rows are dropped from classified_spend (324 − 25 = 299 landed rows, kind distribution contains only charge and refund), so no transfer reaches a COGS or opex total.
The self-check read-back prints `distribution classified_spend.month: '2026-02'=54, '2026-06'=52, ...`, confirming a month column is materialized from txn_date.

The agent chose option (b) — no conversion, currency kept as a dimension (distribution classified_spend.currency) — and recorded the absent rates as a status=blocked row in the landed nxd_decisions model rather than inventing a rate.

The merchant→category ruling lives in data/merchant_categories/merchant_categories.csv as a base model joined in the transform, and self-check phase D ('rulings land as editable data, not transform literals') passed.
Monzo is deliberately left unmapped and lands in an explicit needs_review bucket (41 rows) visible as a value of the category dimension, so question 3 is a plain dimension query.

The transform's reconciliation re-reads the source CSV independently and compares per-currency signed totals with the transfer exclusion as the itemized divergence term — the agent replicated it inline (EUR/USD/GBP expected == derived, 299 == 299) and the phase-B dry-run executed it without failure.

The bucket counts reconcile to the full non-transfer row set (opex 147 + cogs 111 + needs_review 41 = 299 = derived rows expected 299), showing every row lands in exactly one bucket including the unclassified one.
The agent verified txn_id is unique/non-null over 324 source rows and the derived-model check printed `unique keys True` for the landed classified_spend key.

data/nxd_decisions/nxd_decisions.csv lands 3 rows with decision_id,status,ruling,applies_to,detail — merchant categories as proposed, transfer exclusion as confirmed, currency as blocked — and no DECISIONS.md prose file was written.

Netting (signed burn_amount), transfer exclusion (rows removed), monthly regrain (month column) and classification (category column) are all materialized in classified_spend, leaving only measure/dimension selection to the caller.

The agent read models-example.md's explicit warning that description= must go inside dimension() rather than on field(), and the ruling-created dimensions (category, kind, currency) all surface in the phase-A/read-back catalog output without any structural fault.

nxd_decisions is declared as its own semantic model with a metrics view in models.py/spec.py and lands its decision_id/status/ruling/applies_to/detail columns as catalog-visible fields, which the phase-A structural check accepted.

Phase A's structural check against the pinned DSL surface passed with 4 semantic_model / 3 semantic_view entries and only the expected PHYSICAL_MODELS note, and every promised column appears in the read-back distributions rather than as an unroled bare type.

checks.why: The trace shows `cat inferred_model.json` plus `head -5`/full `cat` of both `data/orders/orders.csv` and `data/customers/customers.csv` (and key uniqueness/null probes) before any Write call.

All six required files were written (`spec.py`, `models.py`, `infra-profile.yaml`, `transform/main.py`, `requirements.txt`, `csv-source-path` containing `data`), the final `find` listing shows no forbidden YAML, and the harness printed `PASS python-only-files` and `PASS no-source-yaml`.
The harness digest checks `PASS csv-preserved:customers/customers.csv` and `PASS csv-preserved:orders/orders.csv` confirm the supplied CSVs were untouched byte-for-byte.

The agent verified `order_id` and `customer_id` are unique and non-null over the full export, declared `field(string(), primary_key())` in `models.py`, and the harness printed `PASS promised-primary-keys` and `PASS promised-base-primary-key-tuples`.

The inferred model contains only the two physical base models with no derivation requested, so no derived model exists to mis-key; `PASS physical-models-match-data-dirs` confirms every promised physical model maps to a supplied data directory.
Vacuously satisfied with no derived models, and the harness confirmed the DDL ban held anyway with `PASS no-direct-duckdb-ddl` and `PASS no-out-of-port-write`.
No derived resources were authored, and the harness still printed `PASS derived-resources-flat` and `PASS no-child-tables` over the landed data.
No derived model was introduced, so there is no source-vs-derived relationship left ungated; the transform's read-back naming assertion passed as `PASS transform-contract`.

`models.py` imports only `semantic_model`, `semantic_view`, `field`, `primary_key`, `dimension`, `join`, `metric`, `metric_field`, and `Agg` from public `nxd.spec`, and the harness printed `PASS public-semantic-dsl` and `PASS no-private-semantic-metadata`.

The harness printed `PASS annotations-carried-through` and `PASS inferred-semantic-roles`, which the quoted checker code enforces by requiring each supplied role description to be present on the matching placed role.

The checker section shown in the trace applies `has_description(call)` to the `dimension(...)`/metric role call itself (a `description=` on the enclosing `field(...)` would not satisfy it), and that check passed.

`spec.py` promises `customers`/`orders`, registers `customers_metrics`/`order_metrics` via `.model(...)`, and the harness printed `PASS models-promised`, `PASS desktop-wiring`, `PASS duckdb-port`, and `PASS no-semantic-tools`.

`transform/main.py` declares `BASE_MODELS`/`DERIVED_MODELS`/`PHYSICAL_MODELS` explicitly rather than listing `data/`, and the harness printed `PASS physical-model-declaration` and `PASS physical-models-match-data-dirs`.

The transform uses dlt through `DuckDbOutput` with the source from `secrets["csv_source"]`, an explicit promised-model read-back assert, and a `.transform-complete` touch, confirmed by `PASS transform-contract`, `PASS loaded:customers`, `PASS loaded:orders`, and `PASS transform-complete`.
The agent ran the exact pinned `uv run --python 3.12 ... check_generated_closure.py` command and the output ends with `ALL CHECKS PASSED`.
The final answer states the check validated structurally and executed the transform against a scratch DuckDB and explicitly disclaims any supervisor build or live semantic query.

verdict.summary: The agent read both inputs first, authored a correct Python-only closure with real primary keys and public-DSL descriptions placed inside the role builders, obtained `ALL CHECKS PASSED` from the shipped acceptance check, and reported the result honestly without claiming a supervisor build.
